top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a specific, mature, well-delimited achievement: magic-wavelength trapping of neutral atoms removes the lattice light shift, and Katori's concept and first realisation together with Ye's strontium clock at fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 have been reproduced and compared across independent national laboratories. It has concrete consequences (tests of constant fundamental parameters and relativity, relativistic geodesy, a basis for redefining the second) and the two-laureate allocation is clean and fits the three-person limit without arbitrary exclusion. A citation scoped to the lattice clock separates it from the 2005 frequency-comb prize. Awarding it is clearly preferable to no award.
recusal_note: Professional proximity only: I spent a research stay in John Hall's laboratory, and Jun Ye is a former member of Hall's group; I also work in precision optical spectroscopy. No collaboration with Katori or Ye is apparent from my profile, so no recusal appears required.
